Where you'll be working
Royal Prince Alfred Hospital

What you'll be doing
This position is designed to provide broad exposure to anaesthesia and perioperative medicine and is well suited to junior doctors considering a future career in Anaesthesia or other critical care specialties. Successful applicants will develop clinical skills in anaesthesia, perioperative medicine, pain management and other elements of critical care, while gaining insight into the scope of practice and career pathways within Anaesthesia. Previous experience in anaesthesia is desirable but not essential.

The training year will consist of eight months at RPAH in Sydney and four months at Dubbo Base Hospital, undertaken as four-month rotations. This structure provides valuable experience in both a large tertiary referral centre and a regional hospital environment. Clinical duties will primarily be undertaken in the operating theatre setting under close consultant or provisional fellow supervision. Trainees will participate in the perioperative care of surgical patients and gain experience in:

Administration and monitoring of anaesthesia

Postoperative pain management for surgical patients

Assessment and management of patients in the Post Anaesthesia Care Unit (PACU)

Preoperative assessment of patients in the pre-admission clinic

Participation in the after-hours Acute Pain Service

Throughout the year, trainees will work closely with experienced anaesthetists and will be supported in developing procedural skills, clinical judgement, and a strong foundation in safe perioperative practice. Opportunities to participate in research, audit and quality improvement projects within the departments are encouraged. This role provides an excellent opportunity for junior doctors to gain valuable experience in clinical anaesthesia while exploring potential career pathways in the speciality.

Sydney Local Health District's vision incorporates NSW Health Core Values and a commitment to equity, health improvement, timeliness and efficiency, recognising that evidence-based service delivery requires highly skilled and valued staff supported by research, education and state-of-the-art technologies. 

Our strategic priority under this vision is our commitment to excellence in Patient and Family Centred Care. Staff are supported to ensure patients, their families and carers are considered as partners in care to achieve optimal patient outcomes and best possible healthcare experience.

About our Role

Senior Resident Medical Officer (SRMO) positions in the Eastern & Greater Southern Surgical Skills Training Network - Prince of Wales Hospital (EGSSSTN - POWH) are designed for Junior Medical Officers who are pursuing a career in surgery. These roles provide the opportunity to deliver effective surgical care to patients under supervision in complex clinical environments while supporting preparation for a future surgical career.

SRMOs are expected to develop advanced clinical capability, including the ability to supervise more junior medical officers and, at times, undertake responsibilities aligned with accredited surgical trainees. This may include the assessment and initial management of emergency surgical patients referred for consultations.

SRMOs provide high-quality clinical management of surgical patients across EGSSTN - POWH. Your base hospital will be Prince of Wales Hospital, with rotations across a diverse range of metropolitan and regional network sites. Rotations may include:

Prince of Wales Hospital

General Surgery - including Acute Surgical Unit

Cardiothoracic Surgery

Vascular Surgery

Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery

Surgical Close Observation Unit

Upper GI-Gen Surgery (to be confirmed)

Metropolitan Hospitals

Hand Unit (Sydney and Sydney Eye Hospital)

Paediatric General Surgery - ENT Surgery (Sydney Children's Hospital)

Relief Term (Prince of Wales Hospital and SET trainee relief as required within the POWH-Bankstown General Surgery Network)

Rural-Regional Hospitals

General Surgery (Dubbo Base Hospital)

General Surgery (Griffith Base Hospital)

General Surgery (Bega - South East Regional Hospital)

You will work as a key member of the multidisciplinary team, managing surgical patients and dealing with urgent or sensitive clinical matters with professionalism, discretion, and confidentiality. Clinical decision-making and supervision will be aligned with your level of experience, with increasing independence in patient management expected over time under the guidance of the supervising Attending Medical Officer (AMO). All patients remain under the care of a specialist, and all clinical decisions must be clearly communicated with the responsible consultant.

For further information, please refer to our website: Eastern & Greater Southern Surgical Skills Training Network - POWH (EGSSSTN - POWH)

 

Your Alma Mater

Prince of Wales Hospital and Community Health Services is a major teaching hospital and tertiary referral centre based on the Randwick Hospitals Campus. We provide excellent healthcare to SESLHD and specialist health and medical services to NSW. We connect with various universities, including the University of New South Wales. Our premier medical facilities enable leading learning opportunities for our staff, with the Randwick Campus Redevelopment providing a world-class integrated environment for clinical care, research and education.

Randwick is a metropolitan hub in Sydney's Eastern Suburbs. We have a vibrant, multicultural community, with diverse dining options and regular entertainment hosted by our local council. For those fond of coastal living, we are a walk away from Coogee Beach. A short drive takes you to the famous Bondi Beach and Centennial Parklands. Cycling paths and public transport are readily available, with Sydney's light rail connecting the campus to Sydney's CBD just 7 kilometres away.

 

Perks and Benefits

Come enjoy a blend of urban convenience and relaxed coastal living at Randwick and:

Four weeks of annual leave + an extra Allocated Day Off (ADO) per month if working full time.

Other leave including parental leave, FACS leave, and study & education leave.

Salary Packaging, a way to pay for certain items with your pre-tax salary.

Wellbeing initiatives such as the Employee Assistance Program.

Fitness Passport, a discounted fitness membership for access to nearly 1600 gyms, pools and fitness centres across Australia.

Quality learning and development, research opportunities, and more.

SESLHD is committed to creating a workplace that reflects the diversity of our community. This will help ensure our employees, our patients, and their carers feel supported. We encourage people from different backgrounds to apply.

We welcome applications from Aboriginal and-or Torres Strait Islander candidates and have an Aboriginal Employment Consultant who can support you. If you have any questions or would like guidance on the recruitment process, contact the SESLHD Aboriginal Employment Team via SESLHD-AboriginalWorkforce@health.nsw.gov.au.

MBBS or equivalent, currently registered or eligible for registration with the Medical Board of Australia

A minimum of 2 years of postgraduate experience and previous experience in a surgical department relevant to the position or specialty interest, including sufficient clinical experience in order to undertake the key accountabilities for this role.

Commitment to relevant SET training program: either completed or on track to complete the requirements for admission to SET training. This includes the completion of desired courses, exams and terms.

Demonstrated ability to complete rotations as allocated and required in the Eastern and Greater Southern Surgical Skills Training Network - Prince of Wales Hospital.

Demonstrated ability to work independently within a supervised complex clinical environment utilising excellent clinical skills, judgement and expertise, including demonstrated excellent verbal, written and interpersonal skills, with the capacity to vary communication style.

Demonstrated ability to work collaboratively within multi-disciplinary teams, including the sharing of appropriate information internally and externally with key persons or services.

Demonstrated ability to prioritise workloads and display a flexible approach to meet changing situations in a demanding and unpredictable clinical environment

Demonstrated ongoing commitment to further self-education, professional development and to quality improvement, patient safety and risk management.

Our client MNI ElectroSpark All Trades Services Pty Limited is seeking to add an Accountant to its Greenacre-based operations. The position will support accurate financial reporting, statutory compliance, budgeting, payroll, project costing and management decision-making across a busy multi-trade services environment. The successful appointee will help strengthen financial controls, improve reporting processes and maintain reliable accounting systems as the business continues to grow.

The typical job responsibilities will include, but are not limited to the following:

- Prepare accurate monthly, quarterly and annual financial statements and management reports.
- Manage accounts payable, accounts receivable, payroll processing and general ledger reconciliations.
- Prepare budgets, forecasts and financial models supporting operational and strategic business objectives.

- Maintain and improve accounting systems, reporting tools and automated financial processes.
- Monitor cash flow, outstanding invoices, supplier payments and short-term funding requirements.
- Provide timely financial insights and reports supporting management planning and decision-making.

- Relevant bachelor’s degree or higher qualification in accounting, finance or a closely related professional discipline.

Cox Purtell  
  Senior Salesforce System Administrator  
 You know Salesforce is only as strong as the way it is looked after. 
 Clean access. Sensible configuration. Stable releases. Good support. Strong governance. A platform people can actually rely on. 
 That is what this role is about. 
 You'll be joining a Brisbane-based university using Salesforce across existing and new platforms, including CRM, Marketing and Education Cloud. Some of the environment is established. Some of it is being improved and remediated. Your role will be to help look after the whole platform, not just one narrow part of it. 
 This will suit you if you are a hands-on Salesforce Administrator who likes ownership, cares about platform quality, and enjoys being close to the people who use the system. 
  The role  
 As the Senior Salesforce System Administrator, you'll help keep Salesforce stable, secure and useful across a large university environment. 
 You'll work across day-to-day administration, user support, configuration, platform improvement, release support and governance. 
 You'll be the person helping make sure Salesforce is well managed across CRM, marketing, engagement, alumni-style use cases and Education Cloud. 
 You'll work with the Salesforce Program Manager, architects, business analysts, DevOps specialists and business stakeholders. You won't be working in isolation, but you will be trusted to take real ownership of the admin layer of the platform. 
  What you'll be doing  
 You'll manage Salesforce users, roles, profiles, permission sets, licences and access controls. 
 You'll support Salesforce CRM, Marketing and Education Cloud usage across existing and new platform areas. 
 You'll provide practical support to users, helping resolve issues and improve how teams use Salesforce. 
 You'll configure Salesforce using declarative tools such as Flow, Approval Processes, Assignment Rules, Lightning pages, page layouts and permission structures. 
 You'll support sandbox management, release management and controlled deployment processes. 
 You'll help identify technical debt, platform risks, security issues and improvement opportunities. 
 You'll document changes, support adoption and create guidance that helps users get better value from Salesforce. 
 You'll help improve and remediate the platform while also keeping the current environment running properly. 
  What we're looking for  
 You'll bring strong hands-on Salesforce administration experience. 
 You might currently be a Salesforce Administrator, Senior Salesforce Administrator, Salesforce System Administrator, Salesforce Platform Administrator or Salesforce Consultant with strong admin capability. 
 Higher education experience would be useful, but it is not essential. 
 Experience in adjacent environments would be very relevant, particularly CRM, marketing, membership, alumni, engagement, customer service or stakeholder management platforms. 
 You'll be comfortable working in a complex Salesforce environment where different teams use the platform in different ways. 
 You'll understand Salesforce security, user access, profiles, permission sets, configuration, support and release processes. 
 Salesforce Administrator certification is preferred. If you are not certified yet but are actively working towards it, we are still happy to talk. 
  Why this role could be interesting  
 You'll have genuine ownership of a high-impact Salesforce platform. 
 You'll be involved in both improvement and remediation, not just routine ticket work. 
 You'll work across broad Salesforce use cases, including CRM, Marketing and Education Cloud. 
 You'll be part of a major university environment where Salesforce supports real engagement with students, staff, partners and alumni. 
 You'll have the chance to help create a strong higher-ed Salesforce case study. 
  Location  
 The university is based in Brisbane. 
 Brisbane-based candidates are very welcome and would spend regular time in the office. 
 We can also consider candidates in Sydney, Melbourne or other eastern Australian cities, provided you are willing to travel to Brisbane occasionally. As a guide, there will be an expectation to attend the Brisbane office at least once per month. 
  Work rights  
 We can only consider candidates with full work rights in Australia. 
 You will need to be an Australian citizen, Australian permanent resident or New Zealand citizen. 
  Key details  
 Role: Senior Salesforce System Administrator Platform: Salesforce CRM, Marketing and Education Cloud Contract: 12-month fixed term contract, likely to extend Package: $160,000 plus superannuation Location: Brisbane preferred; Sydney, Melbourne and other eastern Australian cities considered Work rights: Australian citizen, Australian permanent resident or New Zealand citizen only 
  Interested?  
 Apply with your CV or get in touch for a confidential conversation. 
 This is a strong role if you want to own, improve and support a Salesforce platform that matters.

Concord Emergency Department is seeking motivated ACEM Advanced Trainees (AT) to develop a unique skillset on our team.

The Hospital

Concord Repatriation General Hospital is proud of its healthcare service excellence and leadership in clinical care. Concord is part of a network of hospitals and healthcare services within Sydney Local Health District and offers a comprehensive range of specialty and sub-specialty services in the inner-western suburbs of Sydney.

Concord Hospital is committed to ensuring the community has equitable access to high quality patient-centred care that is timely, evidence-based, culturally appropriate and efficient. The hospital provides this care in partnership with highly skilled and committed staff.

The Department of Emergency Medicine

The Emergency department has 2 resus bays, 16 acute beds, a rapid access and fast track area and a new 5-bed ED short stay unit due for completion in late 2026. A high-end CT scanner has been installed adjacent to the resuscitation bays with a co-located radiology department.

Our department is a receiving centre for major burns, a primary PTCA centre for STEMI and is an acute stroke service referral centre. Our patient population is a cohort with complex medical conditions and high acuity presentations and a small proportion of paediatric attendances.

Concord ED is a major referral site and is accredited for 24 months of advanced ED training with Australasian College of Emergency Medicine (ACEM). We provide opportunities to get involved in research and quality assurance activities and encourage consolidating the practice of evidence-based medicine.

The role

As an ED AT you will be part of the dynamic team providing emergency care under the guidance of Emergency Consultants. We will provide you with the opportunity to develop a broad range of clinical skills in a well-supported environment to progress in your career in emergency medicine focussed on medical complexity and high acuity presentations.

Concord ED has an established program for professional development and structured education. We pride ourselves on providing you with a supportive educational environment and flexibility to meet your professional development needs and training goals. This includes:

 Weekly ED registrar teaching (5-hours paid protected time)

 Rotations to develop specialised skills in anaesthetics, intensive care, trauma at Royal Prince Alfred Hospital, paediatrics (ED or ward) at Canterbury Hospital as well as ultrasound, burns and Geriatric Emergency Medicine (GEM) special skills terms

 Dedicated fellowship examination preparation program delivered by an enthusiastic team of consultants.

 Candidate or participant role in Concord ED bi-annual trial OSCE

 Point of Care Ultrasound education

 Clinical audit opportunities to develop a non-clinical portfolio

 Mentorship and career development support to join specialty training programs

 Bedside teaching program including procedural skills accreditation for sedation and central access

 In-situ interprofessional simulation program

 ACEM Associateship training program in Emergency Medicine as an alternative to ACEM training.

 A supportive, collegiate, and diverse work environment

 Convenient location near transport facilities with onsite parking available.

 Salary packaging and fitness passport for eligible staff including utilising SLHD gym facilities

 Wellbeing, advocacy, mentorship, and support opportunities exclusively for medical staff through SLHDs multifaceted workplace program MDOK

 Burns (special skills term)

This unique ACEM accredited rotation consists of a 0.5 Burns and a 0.5 ED component over a 6-month term. It is the only one of its kind in Australia! The ED burns registrar is integrated into the burns team and involved in all aspects of burns care. This provides opportunity to develop special clinical skills, teaching and quality improvement work.

Ultrasound (special skills term)

This rotation enables consolidation of advanced ultrasound skills under the guidance of dedicated supervisors. It is made up of a 0.5 ultrasound and a 0.5 ED component over a 6-month term. Trainees will be supported to accomplish accreditation in multiple CCU units and integrate ultrasound skills in practice.

Anaesthetics and ICU

There are 3-month terms available at CRGH for ICU and anaesthetics that would allow an advanced trainee to satisfy part of the critical care component of FACEM training.

About the Opportunity

Inspire, educate and shape the next generation of nurses in a modern and progressive surgical environment. An exciting permanent part-time opportunity is available for a Clinical Nurse Educator to join our growing Surgical Services team. Based within a modern facility close to Newcastle, you'll support three surgical wards while playing a key role in developing the knowledge, confidence and clinical capability of our nursing workforce. Working within a collaborative education team, you'll be supported by experienced Nurse Educators, fellow Clinical Nurse Educators and nursing leaders who are committed to fostering a culture of continuous learning and professional excellence. This role offers excellent opportunities to further develop your leadership, education and clinical skills, with ongoing support for continued professional development and education. If you're passionate about coaching others, promoting evidence-based practice and making a lasting impact on patient care through education, we'd love to hear from you.

What You Will Be Doing

As a Clinical Nurse Educator, you will lead and support education initiatives across the surgical wards to ensure staff are equipped with the knowledge, skills and confidence to deliver safe, high-quality patient care.
In this role, you will:

Deliver clinical education and bedside teaching to nursing staff.

Support orientation, competency assessments and ongoing professional development.

Identify learning needs across the wards and develop targeted education strategies.

Design, implement and evaluate education programs that promote evidence-based practice.

Mentor and coach staff to build clinical capability and confidence.

Collaborate with Nurse Managers, Clinical Nurse Specialists and multidisciplinary teams to support workforce development.

Contribute to quality improvement initiatives and support the implementation of new clinical practices and models of care.

This role offers the opportunity to influence clinical excellence while supporting the ongoing growth of a skilled and capable nursing workforce.

About you

You are an experienced Registered Nurse with a passion for education, mentoring and developing others. You enjoy building capability within teams and are committed to creating positive learning environments that support both staff and patient outcomes. Our ideal candidate is an excellent communicator who is organised, approachable and confident working collaboratively across multidisciplinary teams. You are proactive in identifying education needs and motivated to develop innovative learning opportunities that strengthen clinical practice. Experience within surgical services is highly desirable, and previous experience as a Clinical Nurse Educator or in a nursing education role will be highly regarded. However, if you have a strong clinical background, a passion for teaching and are looking to transition into education, we encourage you to apply.

Essential Requirements

Current registration as a Registered Nurse with AHPRA.

Demonstrated commitment to evidence-based practice and clinical excellence.

Strong communication, coaching and interpersonal skills.

Ability to develop, deliver and evaluate clinical education.

Commitment to supporting staff development and lifelong learning.

Desirable

Experience working within surgical services.

Previous experience as a Clinical Nurse Educator or similar education role.

Postgraduate qualifications in Clinical Education, Nursing Education or a related field (or working towards).
